kf: NICE NG198: first-line acne treatment is a **12-week fixed-combination topical** (adapalene + benzoyl peroxide, tretinoin + clindamycin, or BPO + clindamycin).
Add an oral **tetracycline (lymecycline or doxycycline)** with a topical for moderate–severe acne; never use oral and topical antibiotics together.
The **combined oral contraceptive (COC)** is an alternative or add-on for women; choose using **UKMEC** (VTE, migraine with aura, smoking over 35).
Co-cyprindiol has higher VTE risk: use only if other options fail and stop 3 months after acne control.
Review at 12 weeks; refer scarring, severe or persistent acne for isotretinoin.
myths: **"The pill causes acne"**: progestogen-only methods can worsen acne; combined pills usually improve it.
patho_lead: The COC reduces acne by **lowering free androgen**, which drives sebum production.

mech.t: Ethinylestradiol and progestogen suppress ovulation and ovarian androgen output.
Oestrogen increases sex hormone–binding globulin, reducing free testosterone.
Lower androgen activity shrinks sebaceous output and comedone formation.
mech.cap: Acne develops from microcomedone to inflamed lesion.

mech.t: Cyproterone, drospirenone and others block androgen receptors.
mech.cap: Hormonal pattern acne along the jawline.

comp: VTE (higher with co-cyprindiol, drospirenone, desogestrel than levonorgestrel), breakthrough bleeding, mood change.
